dialog.body: City of Newport Finance Department, this is Janet Whitcomb. How may I help you?
Hi hon, yeah, Rocco DeLuca here. I'm calling for my mother, she got a bill in the mail, says it's a car tax, and I'm lookin' at it and I don't get it.
Certainly, Mr. DeLuca. What does the bill say? Is it labeled a motor vehicle excise tax?
Yeah, that, excise. Motor vehicle excise. It's got a Buick on it. Problem is, she sold that Buick last year. Like, last spring, maybe May. So why's she gettin' a bill for it?
I see. Do you have the bill in front of you? Is there a bill number or a plate number printed on it?
Hold on, let me find my glasses. [pause] Okay, I got 'em on my head, of course. Plate, yeah, it's got a plate here. You want me to read it?
Not necessary just yet. First, can you tell me what year is shown on the bill? Which tax year or billing year?
Uh, it says, hang on, it says the year is, so it's this year's bill, but the car was sold last year. So that's what I'm sayin'. Wait, is it for this year or last year? It's got two dates on it.

There is typically a registration year and a date of issue. Excise bills are generally based on the registration of the vehicle. If the vehicle was registered to your mother at any point during that period, a bill may be generated even if it was sold later.
Okay, but she sold it. Somebody drove it away. I don't see how she owes on a car she don't have.
I understand. The question is what happened with the registration and plates. When the car was sold, did she cancel the registration with the Registry of Motor Vehicles and return the plates?
Um. Plates. Hon, I honestly don't know. The guy who bought it, he was gonna take care of it, I think. She just signed the thing, the title, and handed him the keys.

I see. If the registration was never canceled, the record could still show her as the owner for part of the period. Generally, the sale paperwork and proof of plate cancellation are what the assessor's office would look at.
The assessor. Okay, so that's not you, that's somebody else?
That's correct. Finance handles billing and payments. Questions about the assessment itself, including whether the vehicle should have been on the roll, go to the assessor's office.
Gotcha. So what are their hours? Like, can I just go down there?
The assessor's office keeps regular weekday hours at City Hall. I would suggest you call ahead to confirm the exact times before making a trip, as I don't want to give you the wrong closing time.
Okay, so weekdays. Not like Saturdays or nothin'.
No, not Saturdays, as a general matter. I can transfer you to that office now if you would like to ask them directly.

Yeah, hold on, one second, before you do that. Is this a different tax than her house tax? Cause she's also got a house bill, and I'm lookin' at both here and they're from the same place but they look different.
Yes, they are separate. The property tax bill is for real estate. The excise bill is for vehicles. They are issued and calculated separately.
So, if I pay the house one, that don't cover the car one.
Correct. Each bill stands on its own.
Okay. Okay, so the car one, I should not pay it yet, or should I? I don't want it goin' to some, you know, late thing.

That is a fair concern. Interest can accrue on unpaid excise bills. That is why I would recommend contacting the assessor's office promptly, today if possible, and bringing the bill of sale and anything showing the plates were turned in.
The bill of sale. See, I don't know if she has one. She's got the, what do you call it, the copy of the title maybe. My sister was helpin' her with that stuff.
A copy of the title or any record of the buyer's name and the sale date would be helpful.

Okay. My sister, she'd know. Except she's got my charger. I let her borrow my phone charger at Christmas, and I never got it back, so now I'm buyin' a new one. Anyway, that's another story. I'll call her.
Very well. Would you like me to transfer you to the assessor's office?
Yeah, but wait. What if it's after, like, they're closed already? It's almost three, right?
It is nearly three o'clock. I cannot tell you with certainty when they close for the day. If no one answers, you can leave a message with your name and number, and they will return your call.
Okay. And the number I'd leave, it's four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-nine-nine. That's the landline, hon, my mother's phone, I'm at her place.
Thank you. And the name on the bill, please? So they can find the account.
Oh, it's under my mother, but I'd have to read it. Hold on. [pause] Hm, it's tiny print. I'll just give 'em the bill number when they pick up.
That will be fine. Please keep the bill beside you. I'll transfer you now, Mr. DeLuca.
Thanks, Janet, you're a doll. So wait, I say it's about the excise and the Buick, right?
Yes. Tell them you are calling about a vehicle excise bill for a vehicle sold last year. Please hold while I connect you.
Okay, holdin'. Thanks again.
